title: Earth's Motions: Rotation, Revolution, and the Making of Seasons

questions.question: Earth's rotation takes about:
questions.rationale: One rotation relative to the stars (sidereal day) is 23 h 56 min 4 s; the 24-hour solar day is longer because Earth also advances along its orbit.

questions.question: The primary cause of Earth's seasons is:
options: Earth's changing distance from the Sun
The 23.5° axial tilt combined with revolution
questions.rationale: The tilt changes the Sun's angle and day length through the year; Earth is actually closest to the Sun (perihelion) in January, during Northern winter.

questions.question: On 21 June, the Sun's rays strike vertically at:
questions.rationale: At the June solstice the Northern Hemisphere tilts fully sunward, putting the vertical ray at the Tropic of Cancer — the northernmost overhead position.

questions.question: At the equinoxes, which statement is true?
options: Day is longer than night everywhere
Day and night are of equal length everywhere
Only the poles see the Sun
The Sun is overhead at 45° latitude
questions.rationale: Around 20 March and 23 September the circle of illumination passes through the poles, giving ~12 hours of daylight at every latitude, with the Sun overhead at the equator.

questions.question: Perihelion (Earth closest to the Sun) occurs around:
questions.rationale: Perihelion is about 3 January (147 million km); aphelion is about 4 July (152 million km).

questions.question: The Coriolis effect, a consequence of rotation, deflects moving objects:
options: To the right in the Northern Hemisphere, left in the Southern
To the left in both hemispheres
questions.rationale: Rotation makes long-range motions curve right (NH) or left (SH), steering trade winds, cyclones, and ocean currents.

questions.question: IST (Indian Standard Time, UTC+5:30) is referenced to which longitude?
questions.rationale: IST uses the meridian 82.5° E (passing near Mirzapur, UP), 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of UTC — one zone for the whole country.

questions.question: Eclipses do not occur every month because:
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted ~5° to the ecliptic, so shadows usually miss
questions.rationale: The lunar orbit is inclined to the ecliptic; only when the new/full Moon is near a node (eclipse season, roughly twice a year) can the shadows align.

questions.question: During a lunar eclipse:
options: Earth's shadow falls on the full Moon
The Sun's shadow falls on Earth
questions.rationale: Earth between Sun and Moon casts its shadow on the full Moon; refracted red light gives the 'blood moon' colour, and it is safe to watch directly.

questions.question: The 41,000-year and 100,000-year Milankovitch cycles involve:
options: Changes in Earth's tilt and orbital eccentricity, pacing ice ages
questions.rationale: Milankovitch identified cyclic changes in axial tilt (~41,000 yr), orbital shape (~100,000 yr), and precession (~26,000 yr) that together pace the glacial ages.
